newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas rises again in West due to heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas rises again in West due to heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were little changed Tuesday as the upcoming Independence Day holiday created a quiet aftermarket and milder weather moved into the Northeast, industry sources said.
However, sweltering heat in western Texas and parts of the Southwest boosted Permian basin prices by another three cents to about $2.03-2.06.
Similarly at the southern California border prices edged two cents higher to about $2.18.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit remained off line and was expected to return to service around July 15.
Meanwhile, San Juan prices were quoted at $2.00-2.03.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted one cent lower at $2.14-2.17 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate were quoted slightly weaker in the low-to-mid $2.40s as cooler weather arrived in the region.
In the Midwest, swing prices rose another cent to about $2.03-2.05.
However, Chicago city-gate was talked lower around $2.20 as more moderate weather pressured cooling demand.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 75 to 100 bcf.
